newsitem.title: USA: Commander of Aberdeen sex sergeants suspended.
newsitem.headline: Commander of Aberdeen sex sergeants suspended.

text.p: The commander of a training unit at the scandal-plagued Aberdeen Proving Ground has been suspended from his post just days before he was due for a transfer, a base spokesman confirmed Wednesday.

The officer, Lt. Col. Martin Utzig, had been commander of the 143rd Ordnance Batallion at the base's Ordnance Centre and School. Seven of 12 trainers charged with sexual misconduct at the school had belonged to the batallion.
"He was suspended from his command Friday," spokesman Ed Starnes said of Utzig. "There are no criminal charges involved. It is purely administrative."

The grounds for the suspension were unclear and it was not known whether the action was related to the pending release of a report by the Army's inspector general on the command environment at Aberdeen, Starnes said.

Utzig was notified of the suspension in a letter from Gen. William Hartzog, commander of the Army's Training and Doctrine Command, which oversees the school, Starnes said. The letter gave Utzig an opportunity to respond as to whether he should be removed from his command of the batallion.

Utzig, who has held the post since July 1995, was due to be transfered to a new command Wednesday under normal military rotation and he can still be given a new command even if he is formally removed from his Aberdeen post, Starnes said. If he is removed from the command, the action would be noted on his military record, Starnes said.

Of seven soldiers from the batallion charged in the scandal, four have been convicted or left the military in lieu of court martial and three are awating trial. The group includes Staff Sgt. Delmar Simpson, convicted in April of 18 counts of rape while serving as a drill instructor.
